subject: Burst clearinghouse credit & staged overrun resolution
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@clearsend.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 17:17:00 -0700
Subject: Burst clearinghouse credit & staged overrun resolution

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for walking me through the ClearSend launch metrics this morning. I dug into the usage spikes you sent over (attached) and ran them against our short-window billing model. Two quick summaries up front:

- ClearSend exceeded the committed QPS threshold on three discrete days in April; total overrun volume across those days maps to roughly 18% above the committed band for the month.
- We can offer a staged resolution that avoids a one-off large invoice while keeping unit economics reasonable for both sides: a three-month clearinghouse credit that offsets 70% of the overrun on month 1, 40% on month 2, and 10% on month 3, paired with a small temporary uplift to your committed tier starting June 1.

Proposal attached: "proposed_staged_credit_term.pdf" (summary + math). Key asks from my side to make this operational:
1) A short PO or e-mail confirmation from Procurement agreeing to the staged schedule so we can lock the invoice path.
2) A commitment to a small monthly upward bump (nominally +15% commit) while the clearinghouse runs, to ensure capacity predictability.
3) Agreement that any sustained run-rate above the bumped commit after the three-month window will be addressed as a contract amendment (we can draft).

If that structure looks reasonable, I can loop in Laura (billing lead) and Ben (commercial) to produce a clean one-page amendment and an invoice schedule that recognizes the credit.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[attachment: clearsend_usage_q1.csv (csv)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@clearsend.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst clearinghouse credit & staged overrun resolution

Marcus—

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the credit construct. The staged approach is attractive because it smooths our cashflow during a tough month. A couple questions from Procurement/Billing:

- Why 70/40/10 vs 50/30/20? (we're parsing the reason for heavier front-loading)
- Is the temporary +15% commit a hard requirement or negotiable? We want to avoid an ongoing price increase if possible.

Procurement would rather sign a short MOU/PO than a long amendment today; that should be fast. On the attachment — our finance team will reconcile the CSV against our internal meter before confirming.

Can you have a draft PO-text and a one-line MOU prepared? That helps us move quickly. If it's fine, I can provide a short-term PO and billing contact details so we can get the invoices queued.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Operations
ClearSend AI

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@clearsend.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst clearinghouse credit & staged overrun resolution

Alyssa —

Thanks. Quick answers before I drop the draft text:
- Front-loading (70/40/10) reflects where the billing pain is concentrated — the first month contains two peak events and a larger share of token volume. It also reduces the collection burden for you in month 1 (biggest relief) while still moving the book toward normal run-rate. We can consider 60/30/10 if you prefer a middle ground; I'll note that in the draft.
- The +15% commit is flexible. We proposed it to ensure throughput headroom while avoiding repeated throttles; we can make it a short-term uplift that automatically rolls back at the end of the three months unless you choose to keep it. If Procurement wants a cap on duration (three months) and a clear rollback clause, that's acceptable.

Attached: a one-page MOU/PO-text stub and the proposed staged schedule embedded in a single PDF. Also included a sample invoice schedule that shows the credit application line by line.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement issues a short PO referencing the MOU stub (I can send language you can paste into your PO).
2) We issue a credit note for month 1 when the PO is received and meter is reconciled.
3) Billing queues the staggered credit for subsequent months, with clear memo lines so accounting matches.

Laura/Ben/Jasmine — please review the attached and confirm we can implement the credit notes as proposed and whether we need legal sign-off on a one-page MOU vs. a full amendment.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed_staged_credit_term.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Burst clearinghouse credit & staged overrun resolution

Marcus/Team —

I reviewed the PDF. A few operational/legal notes:

- We can accept a one-page MOU as long as the PO explicitly references the MOU and the invoice memo lines contain the MOU ID. This avoids a full contract amendment and speeds execution.
- Finance prefers the credit be recorded as a contra-invoice line item and not as a separate refund; that preserves clear audit trails. Laura, can we confirm internal GL code for this?
- We should include a single sentence granting Redwood the right to pause the clearinghouse if ClearSend's post-bump run-rate exceeds the bumped commit by >25% for two consecutive billing cycles — this protects capacity for other customers. Ben will drive the minimal language.

I'll draft the three-sentence legal line and hand it to Marcus to append to the MOU stub.

Ben Carter
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
